<span class="course-code">AGST 50104</span>

# Syllabus

The course develops the ability to choose experimental designs, formulate fixed- and random-effect models, conduct ANOVA and mixed-model analyses, evaluate assumptions, and communicate results in agricultural and biological research.

## Course objectives

By the end of the course, students should be able to:

1. Apply replication, randomization, and blocking to plan valid experiments.
2. Select an appropriate CRD, RCBD, factorial, split-plot, or incomplete-block design.
3. Translate research hypotheses into models with correctly specified fixed and random effects.
4. Conduct ANOVA, linear mixed-model, and generalized linear-model analyses with appropriate diagnostics.
5. Distinguish statistical significance from practical importance and communicate the results.
6. Recognize pseudoreplication, confounding, and incorrect error terms.

## Assessment

| Component | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Weekly homework | 30% |
| Exam I | 15% |
| Exam II | 15% |
| Comprehensive final exam | 20% |
| Final project | 20% |

## Homework workflow

Homework is completed in semester-long groups. The written Quarto submission is due Thursday at 11:59 PM, followed by a short Friday lab presentation by a randomly selected group member. Exact dates and exceptions follow the instructor's course announcements.

## Group project

The final project was completed by a team of four and focused on **Balanced Incomplete Block Designs and Alpha Designs**. The team developed a slide presentation, recorded the presentation, published the video on YouTube, and shared it with the professor for grading.
